info.desc: "10,000 Days" is the fourth studio album by the American rock band Tool. It was released by Tool Dissectional and Volcano Entertainment on April 28, 2006, in parts of Europe, April 29 in Australia, May 1 in the United Kingdom, and May 2 in North America. This album marked the first time since recording "Undertow" in 1993 that the band worked at Grandmaster Recorders and did not collaborate with producer David Bottrill. "10,000 Days" produced three top ten rock singles: "Vicarious", "The Pot", and "Jambi". The album debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 chart, selling 564,000 copies in .

podcast.body: The album was released on April 28, 2006. At the time of the transcript's recording, it had been approximately 11 years and five months since its release. Its release preceded the introduction of the iPhone by over a year, and occurred in the same year NASA launched the New Horizons probe towards Pluto, highlighting the significant time elapsed without new material. "That record came out on April 28th of 2006."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album is the source of a unique "do-it-yourself, three-dimensional song" created by layering three separate tracks. The title track, "10,000 Days" (11:13), when played simultaneously with "Wings for Marie" (6:11) and then immediately followed by "Viginti Tres" (5:02) — with the latter two's combined length exactly matching the title track — creates a perfectly meshed, multi-movement new song, described as brilliant and "beyond awesome." "It's basically a do-it-yourself, three-dimensional song from the 10,000 days album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was released by Tool in 2006. The 13-year, five-month, and three-day gap between "10,000 Days" and "Fear Inoculum" meant that when the former was released, the iPhone had not yet been released, Google had not yet bought YouTube, and MySpace was still a prominent social media platform. "When Tool released the 10,000 days album back in 2006, the iPhone hadn't been released yet."

podcast.body: This was Tool's fourth full album, released at the end of April 2006. Following its release, the band embarked on extensive tours, performing in 2006, 2007, 2008, and 2009. "It was called 10,000 Days, released like I said at the end of April of 2006."
